name: Sarazm valley / terrace context
summary: A raised cultivated terrace above a river corridor, with riparian woody growth and scattered dryland shrubs. The source identifies collected wood taxa, not the exact position of ancient trees or houses.
scaleNote: Landscape dimensions are illustrative. No measured settlement boundary, population or georeferenced ancient watercourse is asserted.

features.label: Vegetation & cultivation
features.text: Sarazm charcoal includes riparian and dryland woody taxa: willow/poplar, ash, Russian olive, tamarisk, hackberry, wild almond, pistachio and juniper, with reeds. High Pamir vegetation is predominantly open. Report pages 7.

features.label: Water & landform
features.text: A cultivated foothill terrace and a high arid lake catchment are different environments. Meltwater and wetland changes need not mirror rainfall or forest extent. Report pages 7.

features.label: What is not reconstructed
features.text: Collected charcoal is not a census of trees growing at each modeled point. Lower-valley woodland loss cannot all be dated before 300 BCE. No species inventory is supplied for this scene; no animated wildlife or livestock has been added. Report pages 7.
